squawks.headline: Trump says Russia wants to reach a deal after the latest talks on Ukraine
squawks.detail: US President Donald Trump said Russia would like to get a deal done following the latest round of talks on ending the war in Ukraine.

squawks.headline: BoE's Greene repeats her call for higher rates, citing bigger-than-expected inflation risks from the Iran war energy shock
squawks.detail: Reuters reports that MPC member Megan Greene said the risk of broader inflation from the energy price shock linked to the Iran war is greater than the Bank expected. She repeated her view that interest rates should rise.

squawks.headline: Rubio says Iran's actions against commercial shipping are unlike anything seen since the Second World War
squawks.detail: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio described Iran's conduct towards commercial vessels as unmatched since the Second World War.

squawks.headline: Rubio says a deal with Iran is extremely hard to reach because hardliners control Tehran
squawks.detail: US Secretary of State Rubio said reaching an agreement with Iran is extremely difficult because hardliners are in control there. He spoke as US-Iran talks continue through Pakistani and Qatari mediation.

squawks.headline: Trump says he must make a final decision on Iran, winning either the nice way or the not-so-nice way
squawks.detail: The US President said Washington has to decide one way or the other on Iran. He also said he has to choose how the US wins against Tehran, by friendly means or otherwise.

squawks.headline: US Energy Department commits about $967m in extra funding for power grid upgrades to curb rising electricity costs
squawks.detail: Reuters reported on Tuesday that the US Department of Energy will invest roughly $967 million in additional funding to modernise critical energy infrastructure. The department said the aim is to lower surging electricity costs.

squawks.headline: US to propose a face-to-face meeting between Putin, Zelenskyy and Trump, Politico reports
squawks.detail: Politico reports that the US will offer Russia's President Putin in-person talks with Ukraine's President Zelenskyy and President Trump. No market reaction has been reported.

squawks.headline: BoE's Greene says there is reason to worry policy is not restrictive enough, with inflation expectations anchored but above norms
squawks.detail: MPC member Megan Greene said there is a need to be concerned that the policy stance is not tight enough. She described inflation expectations as anchored but sitting above their usual levels.

squawks.headline: BoE's Greene says people take notice of inflation once it is above 3% and expects supply shocks to keep coming
squawks.detail: MPC member Megan Greene said public awareness of inflation picks up when it goes above 3%, and that the economy will continue to face many supply shocks. The comments follow her earlier remarks that wage disinflation has stalled.

squawks.headline: BoE's Greene questions the Bank's estimate of pay growth consistent with target, putting it at 3% wage growth for 2% inflation
squawks.detail: MPC member Megan Greene said she has concerns about the Bank of England's estimate of target-consistent pay growth, and said 3% wage growth is consistent with 2% inflation.

squawks.headline: Iran's President Pezeshkian says he believes the US will attack again if Tehran negotiates
squawks.detail: Iran's President Pezeshkian said he believes the US would launch another attack if Iran entered negotiations, Tasnim reported. Pakistan's army chief Munir has left Tehran, Nour News reported.

squawks.headline: Iran's President Pezeshkian tells Pakistani mediator the US must lift all pressure, threats and sanctions before any negotiations
squawks.detail: Iran's President Pezeshkian set this precondition for talks with Washington in remarks to the Pakistani mediator, according to a report. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: PM Burnham plans legislation to reduce the UK benefits bill, possibly as early as April, Telegraph reports
squawks.detail: The Telegraph reports that Prime Minister Burnham plans to bring in legislation to cut the benefits bill, which could be introduced as soon as April. No figures for the savings were given in the reports.

squawks.headline: Finland's President Stubb says the Ukraine peace process is back on track after a week of quiet progress
squawks.detail: Finnish President Alexander Stubb said significant progress had been made out of public view over the past week or so and called the day a good one for peace.

squawks.headline: IEA chief says the agency is ready to coordinate further emergency oil stock releases if needed
squawks.detail: The head of the International Energy Agency said on Tuesday that the agency stands ready to coordinate more emergency oil releases by member countries, while it pushes for diesel to be released under existing plans to ease surging prices, Reuters reports.

squawks.headline: Zelenskyy says the US has set out strong security guarantees in a document that will be shared with Russia
squawks.detail: Speaking at a press conference in Oslo with Nordic leaders, Zelenskyy said US intelligence on missile strikes is working again and that he expects positive results from talks with Rubio on Patriot missiles. Norway's prime minister said Europe needs to be part of talks on the European security order, and Finland's president said it is very important that the US stays engaged.

squawks.headline: Turkey sends defence pact with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan to parliament for ratification
squawks.detail: Three parliamentary sources told Reuters the pact has been submitted, bringing Turkey closer to a formal mutual defence commitment with Riyadh while Saudi Arabia faces Houthi attacks.

squawks.headline: US envoy Witkoff to meet Russian leadership in St Petersburg tomorrow after Oslo talks with Zelenskyy and Nordic leaders
squawks.detail: Norway's prime minister said Witkoff flies to St Petersburg tomorrow, and Finland's president said elements of peace found at the meeting will be taken forward there. Zelenskyy said Ukraine is ready for negotiations and wants to see de-escalation, that security guarantees were discussed, that territorial questions need to be settled at the highest level, and that he hopes to speak to Rubio within 48 hours.

squawks.headline: Russia extends its strikes on Ukrainian energy facilities to western Ukraine, causing waves of blackouts
squawks.detail: Reuters reports, citing Ukrainian energy ministry officials and local authorities, that Russian attacks on energy facilities now reach western Ukraine and have caused repeated blackouts.

squawks.headline: Zelenskyy offers to stop strikes on sensitive Russian energy sites if Russia does the same, and seeks a trilateral leaders' meeting
squawks.detail: After talks with US envoy Witkoff and Norway's prime minister, Ukraine's President Zelenskyy said Kyiv is ready for a mutual halt to strikes on sensitive energy infrastructure and wants to move towards a three-way meeting at leaders' level. He said Witkoff travels to Russia tomorrow, while Norway's prime minister called the talks good and constructive and Finland's President Stubb said there had been genuine progress.

squawks.headline: BoE's Greene says wage disinflation has stalled above 2%-consistent levels and second-round inflation risk is greater than thought
squawks.detail: MPC member Megan Greene said forward-looking data point to pay growth closer to 3.5%, the economy has been surprisingly resilient and labour market slack may have peaked. She said she still believes the MPC should lean proactively against the risk of second-round inflation effects.

squawks.headline: Iran's top security official Rezaei tells Pakistan's army chief Munir there will be no talks with the US until Tehran's conditions are met
squawks.detail: Iran's top security official gave the message to Pakistan's army chief, who has been carrying a compromise proposal in the US-Iran talks.

squawks.headline: Lavrov says Russia will hear US envoys Witkoff and Kushner's proposals but will make no political concessions
squawks.detail: Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov says Moscow will look at what US envoys Witkoff and Kushner put forward, but will not make political concessions.

squawks.headline: Iran's Revolutionary Guards warn ships off unauthorised routes in the Gulf and Sea of Oman and vow decisive action over Hormuz violations
squawks.detail: Iran's Revolutionary Guards say vessel owners and crews are responsible if they use unauthorised routes in the Persian Gulf and Sea of Oman, and that breaches of security in the Strait will be dealt with decisively. The warning follows the Guards' report of a supertanker hitting a mine in the southern Strait of Hormuz.

squawks.headline: Iran's Revolutionary Guards navy says a supertanker carrying more than 2 mln barrels of crude exploded after hitting a mine near Hormuz
squawks.detail: Iranian media, including IRIB News, carried the Revolutionary Guards navy's account. It said the tanker, which it called 'violating', exploded after striking a mine south of the Strait of Hormuz and was carrying over 2 mln barrels of crude. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Iran's security chief rules out talks with the US until Washington builds trust
squawks.detail: Iran's Security Council secretary Rezaei set the condition after meeting Pakistan's army chief, according to Iranian state media IRNA. Separately, Tasnim reported that he said all of Iran's enriched nuclear material will stay in the country.

squawks.headline: France to send troops to back up police for protests planned on 24 October, and admits failures over weekend unrest
squawks.detail: Reuters reports that the French government announced a large security operation for Saturday's protests. The government said its response to last weekend's violence had failed.

squawks.headline: Iran's Security Council secretary says none of Iran's enriched nuclear material will be sent abroad
squawks.detail: Iran's Tasnim news agency reported the remarks by the secretary of Iran's Security Council while US-Iran talks continue.

squawks.headline: France's 20-year bond spread over Germany is already 170bp, says economist Robin Brooks
squawks.detail: Economist Robin Brooks says France's 20-year spread over Germany has reached 170bp. He argues that the 10-year tenor usually watched is the one most affected by ECB action to cap yields.

squawks.headline: Iran tells Pakistan it has nothing new to say to the US, Mehr reports
squawks.detail: Iran's Mehr news agency reports that Tehran has told Pakistan, which has been mediating, that it has no new message for the US. Earlier reports said a compromise proposal carried by Pakistan's army chief had been put forward in the US-Iran talks.

squawks.headline: Iran's parliament speaker Ghalibaf sets seven conditions the US must meet to win Tehran's trust
squawks.detail: Iran's Mehr news agency reported the remarks by parliament speaker Ghalibaf while US-Iran talks continue, on the day Pakistan's army chief met President Pezeshkian in Tehran to discuss mediation. The reports did not list the conditions and gave no market reaction.

squawks.headline: Bank of Israel expected to hold rates on Wednesday after three straight cuts, ahead of the 27 October election, Reuters poll shows
squawks.detail: A Reuters poll shows the Bank of Israel is expected to leave short-term interest rates unchanged on Wednesday after three successive reductions. Respondents expect policymakers to pause before next week's election even though inflation is stable.

squawks.headline: US Energy Secretary Wright says the US is working with India to lift refining output and get more products to market
squawks.detail: US Energy Secretary Wright said the US is working with India to raise refining output so that more products reach the global market. Separately, Secretary of State Rubio said Reliance has an opportunity to help India keep diversifying its energy supply chain.

squawks.headline: Rubio says oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz are close to pre-war levels
squawks.detail: US Secretary of State Rubio said on 20 October that the volume of oil passing through Hormuz is nearly back to where it was before the war. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Rubio expects the US-India trade deal within weeks rather than months, with only technical details left
squawks.detail: US Secretary of State Rubio said he expects to see the trade deal with India in a matter of weeks, and that only some technical details remain to be settled.

squawks.headline: US Energy Secretary Wright says any Russian diesel imported to the US would most likely go to New England
squawks.detail: US Energy Secretary Wright said Russian diesel coming to the US under the proposed US-Russia diesel arrangement would probably be sent to New England. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: US Energy Secretary Wright says diesel prices could fall meaningfully if Europe agrees to a coordinated release
squawks.detail: US Energy Secretary Wright said Europe joining a coordinated release could bring meaningful relief on diesel prices. He also said more work is needed on refining and on Defense Production Act funding.

squawks.headline: Iran-US talks are still going on and reports that a deal is close are wrong, says a person familiar
squawks.detail: An unnamed person said negotiations between Iran and the US continue but denied reports that an agreement is near. The denial follows earlier reports of a compromise proposal put forward by Qatar and Pakistan.

squawks.headline: Mexico's President Sheinbaum says USTR and the Commerce Department are positive on a US-Mexico trade deal
squawks.detail: Mexico's President Sheinbaum said the US Trade Representative and the Commerce Department hold a positive view of the trade deal with Mexico. Earlier she had said a deal was very close but that some issues were still open.

squawks.headline: Trump administration recently came close to approving a strike on Iran, i24NEWS reports
squawks.detail: Israeli broadcaster i24NEWS reports that the US administration recently came close to authorising a strike on Iran. The report comes as US-Iran talks over a compromise proposal continue; no market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: US single-family housing starts fall sharply in September; single-family permits drop to a three-and-a-half-year low
squawks.detail: Reuters reports that US single-family homebuilding fell sharply in September. It says permits for future single-family construction fell to their lowest in three and a half years as higher mortgage rates held back demand.

squawks.headline: Canada's US trade minister says trade talks with the US are continuing and expects a deal eventually
squawks.detail: Canada's minister responsible for US trade said Ottawa is still holding trade talks with its US counterparts. The minister said a deal serving the whole Canadian economy will be reached at some point, but gave no timing.

squawks.headline: Mexico's President Sheinbaum says a trade deal with the US is very close but some issues remain
squawks.detail: Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum said a trade agreement with the United States is very close, though some issues are still to be resolved.

squawks.headline: Netanyahu says he discussed overthrowing Iran's regime with Trump on Monday
squawks.detail: Israel's Prime Minister Netanyahu said he spoke with President Trump on Monday about eliminating the Iranian regime, and said the regime must be overthrown. The remarks come as US-Iran talks on a compromise proposal continue.

squawks.headline: US-Iran compromise proposal would send Iran the interest on $6bn of its funds frozen in Qatari banks, Israel's Channel 12 reports
squawks.detail: Israel's Channel 12 reports that the proposal, which Pakistan's army chief presented to senior Iranian officials, partly meets Iran's demand for the return of its frozen funds. It says the US has approved the plan and Iran has given preliminary agreement.

squawks.headline: US pending home sales drop 7.3% on the month in September against a forecast 0.5% fall; index slides to 66.0
squawks.detail: US pending home sales fell 7.3% month on month, compared with a forecast fall of 0.5% and a 0.3% rise previously. The pending homes index came in at 66.0, down from 71.2.

squawks.headline: US Energy Under Secretary Haustveit says diesel prices are too high and the US is working with refiners to raise output
squawks.detail: US Energy Under Secretary Haustveit said current diesel prices are higher than anyone would want and that officials are working with refiners on ways to increase production.

squawks.headline: China tells the US to revoke restrictions on Chinese firms and vows necessary measures to defend its interests
squawks.detail: China's commerce ministry called on the US to immediately reverse what it described as discriminatory restrictions on Chinese companies. It said China would take necessary measures to protect its interests.

squawks.headline: China's commerce ministry firmly opposes the US order on DeepSeek and calls it discriminatory
squawks.detail: China's commerce ministry says the US order on DeepSeek is discriminatory, politicises tech and trade issues under the pretext of national security, and ignores the consensus reached between the two countries' heads of state.

squawks.headline: French borrowing costs rise further towards 5% as social unrest weighs on the bond market, FT reports
squawks.detail: The FT reports that French government borrowing costs rose again today to close to 5%, amid social unrest in France and fallout in the bond market.

squawks.headline: Bessent says Iran's currency has collapsed and panic is setting in, and calls the energy price spike temporary
squawks.detail: In live remarks, US Treasury Secretary Bessent said Iran's economy would at some point go non-linear and that things were going well despite what he called a temporary spike in energy prices. He also said the US is working hard to end its reliance on Chinese critical minerals, that losing chip supply from Taiwan would be devastating, and that Putin has not yet replied to the G20 invitation.

squawks.headline: Bessent calls for US spending control and faster growth to tackle debt, links higher rates to the energy shock
squawks.detail: US Treasury Secretary Bessent said spending must be brought under control and growth raised to overcome debt. He also said rates are up because of the energy shock, housing has slowed and he expects mortgage rates to come down. He added that any action on Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac would not widen agency debt spreads, and that ownership may be addressed next year.

squawks.headline: US Treasury Secretary Bessent says US bond market and auctions are performing well and sees no spillover from France
squawks.detail: In a TV interview, the US Treasury Secretary said recent bond auctions had been strong, that investors are buying bonds at a price, and that the US is getting past a temporary energy price shock. He also said the US must grow its way out of debt and that he is not seeking another job.

squawks.headline: Italy's PM Meloni condemns the US diesel deal with Russia
squawks.detail: A market commentator reports that Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni has strongly condemned the US diesel arrangement with Russia. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Google restores full service in its London cloud region after an outage that disrupted UK banks
squawks.detail: Alphabet's Google said on Tuesday that full service is back in its London-based cloud region, after a power event disrupted several cloud services, Reuters reports.

squawks.headline: Iran accepts secret IAEA site inspections as part of the compromise proposal in US talks, Al-Araby Al-Jadeed reports
squawks.detail: Al-Araby Al-Jadeed reports that Iran has agreed to secret inspections of sites by the IAEA under the compromise proposal in US-Iran negotiations. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: US-Iran compromise proposal carried by Pakistan's army chief has US and Iranian approval, Al-Araby Al-Jadeed reports
squawks.detail: Al-Araby Al-Jadeed cites sources as saying the new proposal aims to head off escalation and restart talks. It also partly meets Iran's demand over its frozen funds.

squawks.headline: Qatar and Pakistan put forward a compromise proposal in US-Iran talks, Al-Araby Al-Jadeed reports
squawks.detail: Al-Araby Al-Jadeed, citing sources familiar with the mediation, reports that Qatar and Pakistan have presented a compromise proposal intended to meet both US and Iranian demands. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: All 100 economists in a poll expect a Fed rate hike in December; 94 see a hold at the 27-28 October meeting
squawks.detail: In the poll, 94 of 100 economists expect the fed funds rate to stay at 3.75%-4.00% this month and the rest expect a hike to 4.00%-4.25%. 94 of 100 see 4.00%-4.25% by the end of 2026, compared with 29 of 76 in the September poll.

squawks.headline: New EU Arctic strategy aims to keep oil, coal and gas in the ground, including in Arctic regions
squawks.detail: The European Commission says it will work with partners to prevent hydrocarbon reserve developments that threaten the Arctic ecosystem. Commission President von der Leyen says the EU must change its strategic posture in the Arctic.

squawks.headline: Putin floats a US-China-Russia summit with Trump and Xi to negotiate an end to the Ukraine war, WSJ reports
squawks.detail: The Wall Street Journal reports that Russia's President Putin raised the possibility of a three-way summit with the US and Chinese leaders on a deal to end the war in Ukraine, as reported by Semafor. Semafor said Trump already faces criticism from Republicans over his approaches to Putin, including the waiving of sanctions on Russia.

squawks.headline: US building permits come in at 1.4M in September, above the 1.385M forecast; housing starts fall 5.2% on the month
squawks.detail: US September building permits were 1.4M against a 1.385M forecast and 1.403M previously, a 0.2% monthly fall versus an expected 1.3% drop. Housing starts fell 5.2% on the month against a forecast rise of about 2%.

squawks.headline: US housing starts fall to 1.221M in September, short of the 1.305M forecast
squawks.detail: US housing starts came in at 1.221M for September, against a forecast of 1.305M and down from 1.275M the previous month.

squawks.headline: Russian diesel exports head back to former main buyers after the US-brokered lifting of Moscow's export ban
squawks.detail: Reuters reports that Kpler and LSEG shipping data show at least two tankers signalling voyages to Turkey and Brazil in recent days, after Russia's diesel export ban was lifted with US involvement.

squawks.headline: US ADP weekly private payrolls average 18.5K, slowing from 24.75K previously
squawks.detail: ADP says private employers added an average of 18.5K jobs a week in the four weeks to 3 October, down from 24.75K in the previous reading. No forecast was given.

squawks.headline: Gilts outperform G7 peers as investor concern over the UK Budget fades, FT reports
squawks.detail: The Financial Times reports that UK government bonds sold off heavily when the Iran war began but have since done better than other G7 markets. It says traders' focus has moved to France.

squawks.headline: Russia's Ryabkov says Moscow's Ukraine stance does not hinge on Trump postponing severe new sanctions on Russia
squawks.detail: Russia's deputy foreign minister Sergei Ryabkov said Moscow's approach to resolving the war in Ukraine does not depend on the US president's decision to delay what have been described as very severe sanctions on Russia.

squawks.headline: Russia's deputy foreign minister Ryabkov says Moscow still views a possible US-Russia diesel deal positively
squawks.detail: Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Sergei Ryabkov said Moscow still sees the possible diesel deal between Russia and the United States in a positive light. US lawmakers have opposed the proposed deal, and the US Energy Secretary has said no Russian diesel has been released so far.

squawks.headline: Starmer's spokesman rejects the idea that the UK risks being drawn into the Saudi-Houthi war
squawks.detail: The Prime Minister's spokesman said the government does not accept that the UK risks being pulled into the Saudi-Houthi conflict. This follows the UK's decision to fly defensive missions over Saudi Arabia.

squawks.headline: European benchmark gas price rises above €90 for the first time since 2022
squawks.detail: Europe's benchmark gas contract has traded above €90 for the first time since 2022, according to a market report. Middle East supply tensions are already on the blotter.

squawks.headline: Google Cloud outage disrupts UK banks including Halifax and Revolut
squawks.detail: The FT reports that a Google Cloud outage has hit several businesses, including UK lenders Halifax and Revolut. Google says a power outage caused the failure of its Cloud services.

squawks.headline: UK MoD says RAF Typhoons will fly defensive missions only over Saudi Arabia and will not strike the Houthis
squawks.detail: The UK Ministry of Defence says RAF Typhoon jets will fly defensive counter-air missions to help protect Saudi cities and critical national infrastructure from aerial attack. It says the aircraft will not carry out offensive strikes against the Houthis.

squawks.headline: Rubio says India has made substantial progress in diversifying its oil purchases
squawks.detail: US Secretary of State Rubio said India has made substantial progress in diversifying where it buys its oil. He made the remarks while the US and India are working on a trade deal.

squawks.headline: Rubio says Trump is frustrated by accusations that he is harming Ukraine
squawks.detail: US Secretary of State Rubio said President Trump is frustrated by accusations that he is harming Ukraine. Separately, Ukraine's President Zelenskiy has arrived in Oslo for talks with US negotiators.

squawks.headline: Rubio says the war must end through negotiation and backs US, China and Russia arms control talks
squawks.detail: US Secretary of State Rubio said the war must be ended through negotiation and that arms control talks between the US, China and Russia would benefit the world. He also linked energy to national security and said Indian refining of Venezuelan crude would be discussed.

squawks.headline: Rubio says a batch of PURL interceptors for Ukraine may not have been delivered and warns Russia-Ukraine war could escalate
squawks.detail: US Secretary of State Rubio said Trump is disappointed at the lack of progress in Russia-Ukraine talks, that the conflict risks spreading to other places, and that it could be accurate that a batch of interceptors bought for Ukraine under the PURL programme has not been delivered. He also said the US will talk with Reliance about refining more Venezuelan crude.

squawks.headline: UK will fly missions to defend Saudi Arabia against Houthi attacks
squawks.detail: A market newswire reports that the UK will fly missions to help defend Saudi Arabia from Houthi attacks. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Rubio says an India trade deal is close and US policy on Ukraine, including intelligence sharing, is unchanged
squawks.detail: US Secretary of State Rubio said only a few items remain on a trade deal with India. He said he spoke with President Zelenskiy for 45 minutes, that nothing has changed on Pentagon support or intelligence sharing for Ukraine, that the US is not deliberately denying interceptors to Ukraine, and that the US is taking steps to help Saudi Arabia.

squawks.headline: Most Gulf stock markets fall after Houthis claim attacks on Saudi energy, airport and military sites
squawks.detail: Reuters reports that most Gulf bourses fell in early trade on Tuesday after Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis claimed attacks on Saudi energy, airport and military targets on Monday.

squawks.headline: IEA chief Birol says the agency will consider further releases from emergency oil stocks if needed
squawks.detail: Fatih Birol, head of the International Energy Agency, said the agency would look at releasing more oil from emergency stocks if required. No volumes or timing were given.

squawks.headline: ECB policymaker Rehn says the French-German bond spread has widened somewhat
squawks.detail: Olli Rehn, Bank of Finland governor and member of the ECB Governing Council, said the gap between French and German government bond yields has widened to some extent.

squawks.headline: Kremlin says Russia values the work of US negotiators highly
squawks.detail: The Kremlin said on 20 October that Russia rates the efforts of US negotiators highly. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Kremlin hopes Putin can meet US envoy Witkoff in Russia soon and calls for urgent resumption of US nuclear stability talks
squawks.detail: The Kremlin said it hoped a meeting between President Putin and Trump envoy Steve Witkoff could be organised in Russia in the near future, and that US negotiators could brief Putin on the Ukrainian and European positions. It also said dialogue with the US on strategic nuclear stability needs to resume urgently.

squawks.headline: Iran's Revolutionary Guards say mines hit two oil tankers south of the Strait of Hormuz, leaving them on fire and stopped
squawks.detail: The IRGC navy said two tankers struck mines south of the Strait of Hormuz, caught fire and were brought to a halt. Tasnim carried the report, which gave no date for the incident. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: UK 10-year gilt auction yields 5.418% with 3.61 times cover, up from 5.383% and 3.34 at the previous sale
squawks.detail: The 10-year gilt auction produced an average yield of 5.418%, against 5.383% at the previous sale of the line. The bid-to-cover ratio was 3.61, up from 3.34 last time.

squawks.headline: Eurozone construction output rises 1.8% on the month after a flat previous reading
squawks.detail: Eurozone construction output grew 1.8% month on month, following 0.0% in the previous reading. No forecast was given.

squawks.headline: German ZEW economic sentiment falls to 28.1, below 30 forecast; current conditions improve to -35.9
squawks.detail: German ZEW economic sentiment came in at 28.1, down from 34.7 and below the 30 forecast, while current conditions rose to -35.9 from -47.1, beating the -44.5 forecast. Eurozone ZEW expectations fell to 18.5 from 25.8.

squawks.headline: Iran's foreign ministry says Egypt's readiness to help Saudi Arabia in its war with the Houthis is worsening the situation
squawks.detail: A spokesman for Iran's foreign ministry said Egypt's stated readiness to back Saudi Arabia against the Houthis is making the conflict worse. The remarks come after the Houthis claimed attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure.

squawks.headline: Saudi civil defence says the danger in Riyadh has passed after the earlier alert
squawks.detail: Saudi civil defence said the threat in the capital had ended, following its earlier alert when sirens sounded in Riyadh. The inputs report no market reaction.

squawks.headline: Saudi civil defence issues an early alert in Riyadh as sirens sound in the capital
squawks.detail: Saudi civil defence issued an early warning in Riyadh, and sirens were reported in the city. It follows Houthi claims of attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure; no market reaction has been reported so far.

squawks.headline: South Korea's finance ministry says it will consider cutting bond issuance further if needed
squawks.detail: South Korea's finance ministry said it would consider a further cut to government bond issuance if necessary. It gave no figures or timing.

squawks.headline: Eurozone seasonally adjusted current account surplus narrows to €8.7bn in August from €27.6bn
squawks.detail: ECB data show the seasonally adjusted eurozone current account surplus at €8.7bn for August, down from €27.6bn the month before. The unadjusted figure was €7.70bn, against a revised €35.90bn previously.

squawks.headline: Iran says excessive US demands are holding up progress in negotiations
squawks.detail: Iran repeated its position that US demands are blocking progress in talks between the two sides. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: BoJ may lift its inflation forecast for next fiscal year and keep rates on hold this month, sources say
squawks.detail: Four sources familiar with the Bank of Japan's thinking told Reuters it may raise its inflation outlook for the next fiscal year in forecasts due this month. The sources linked this to higher oil prices keeping price pressures in place for longer than expected.

squawks.headline: EU foreign policy chief Kallas says the EU is working with Turkey, India and others on a Black Sea deal
squawks.detail: Kallas said a Black Sea arrangement would protect lives and supplies. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: UAE commits to supplying France with 100k tons of diesel a month; Bahrain and UAE deliveries due in coming weeks
squawks.detail: The United Arab Emirates has committed to provide France with 100k tons of diesel a month, following an earlier Saudi commitment. Deliveries from Bahrain and the UAE to France are reported to start in the coming weeks.

squawks.headline: Saudi Arabia commits to supplying France with 95k tons of diesel a month
squawks.detail: Saudi Arabia has committed to supply France with 95k tons of diesel per month, according to a market news post. No further terms or timing were given.

squawks.headline: Japan's PM Takaichi says she does not intend to put pressure on prices to come down
squawks.detail: Japanese Prime Minister Takaichi said she has no intention of exerting pressure to lower prices. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: UK total pay growth slows to 3.7%, below 3.8% forecast; private-sector regular pay at 3.0%, in line; claimant count up 30.3K
squawks.detail: ONS figures for the three months to August show average weekly earnings including bonuses up 3.7% year on year, against a 3.8% forecast and 3.9% previously. Private-sector regular pay rose 3.0%, as expected, after 2.9%. The claimant count rose 30.3K after 27.8K, with the claimant count rate unchanged at 4.4%.

squawks.headline: German producer prices rise 6.7% year on year, above the 6.3% forecast
squawks.detail: German PPI rose 1.9% month on month against a 1.6% forecast and 1.1% previously. The annual rate rose to 6.7% from 4.6%, against a 6.3% forecast.

squawks.headline: UK unemployment rate falls to 4.7% against a 4.9% forecast; employment up 102K on the quarter
squawks.detail: UK labour market data show the unemployment rate at 4.7%, compared with a forecast and previous reading of 4.9%. Employment rose 102K over three months, against a 5K forecast and 67K previously, and average weekly earnings growth including bonuses slowed to 3.7% from 3.9%, below the 3.8% forecast.

squawks.headline: UK regular pay growth picks up to 3.7%, above 3.6% forecast; employment rises 13K against an expected 8K fall
squawks.detail: UK average earnings excluding bonuses rose 3.7%, compared with a 3.6% forecast and 3.5% previously. Employment rose 13K after a 26K fall in the previous release, and the unemployment change was 30.3K, up from 27.8K.

squawks.headline: Japan's PM Takaichi says she does not expect to seek a mandate after the two-year tax cut
squawks.detail: Japan's Prime Minister Takaichi also denied reports that an income limit of 3M yen had been set for benefits.

squawks.headline: BoJ expected to hold rates in October and signal a possible hike as early as December, sources say
squawks.detail: Sources say the Bank of Japan is likely to keep rates on hold at its 29-30 October meeting while signalling room to raise them as soon as December. The same sources say its quarterly report may nudge up the fiscal 2027 inflation forecast slightly.

squawks.headline: French PM says targeted curfews kept the peace overnight; local authorities will impose more tonight where needed
squawks.detail: France's prime minister said the targeted curfews helped keep the peace overnight. He said curfews would be imposed again tonight wherever the situation requires, with local authorities making those decisions on the ground.

squawks.headline: PBOC considers using the overnight rate as the main anchor of China's monetary policy
squawks.detail: Reports say the People's Bank of China is exploring a shift to the overnight rate as its main policy anchor. An expert quoted by a PBOC-backed news outlet says the change does not signal monetary easing and should not be seen as a rate cut.

squawks.headline: Japan's 40-year JGB yield falls 6bp to 4.05%
squawks.detail: Japan's 40-year government bond yield is reported 6bp lower at 4.05% in Tokyo trading on 20 October.

squawks.headline: UK Treasury expected to study options for closer long-term ties with the EU, FT reports
squawks.detail: The Financial Times reports that the Treasury is expected to carry out a study of Britain moving closer to the EU, with Andy Burnham preparing to set out options for the UK's longer-term relationship with the bloc.

squawks.headline: China sells 10-year government bonds at a 1.6057% yield
squawks.detail: Traders say China's finance ministry auctioned 10-year bonds at a yield of 1.6057%, and offered 2-month bills at 1.0316%.

squawks.headline: Bank of England and Bank of Korea widen their partnership on tokenisation
squawks.detail: Yonhap reports that South Korea's central bank and the Bank of England have broadened their cooperation on tokenisation.

squawks.headline: PBOC to offer up to 1 trillion yuan a day in overnight reverse repos from 21 October to 2 November
squawks.detail: China's central bank announced the overnight reverse repo operations for the period. It carried out no 7-day reverse repos on Tuesday.

squawks.headline: Japan's finance minister Katayama says no decision has been made on how to fund the expected rise in defence spending
squawks.detail: Katayama said the government is still discussing defence spending and will look at ways to secure stable funding while keeping a focus on fiscal sustainability.

squawks.headline: Trump says the US and Mexico are very close to a trade deal
squawks.detail: US President Trump said on Monday that Mexico and the United States are very close to agreeing a trade deal, Reuters reports.

squawks.headline: China keeps its one-year and five-year loan prime rates at 3.00% and 3.50%, as expected
squawks.detail: The People's Bank of China left its benchmark lending rates unchanged in October, in line with forecasts. Reuters reports that rates have now been held for 17 months in a row.

squawks.headline: Japan's economy minister Kiuchi says he hopes to attend this month's BoJ policy meeting if his schedule allows
squawks.detail: Kiuchi said the government respects the Bank of Japan's autonomy over monetary policy as set out in the BoJ law. He also said he has never considered asking for a vote at a BoJ meeting to be postponed.

squawks.headline: US 10-year Treasury yield holds at 5.14% after a 7bp rise; French unrest weighs on European bonds and the euro
squawks.detail: A market wrap reports the US 10-year yield steady at 5.14% after rising seven basis points, with oil near elevated levels on Middle East supply risks. French political unrest was reported as adding pressure to European bonds and the euro.

squawks.headline: Trump says NATO allies refused to help the US in the Iran war and the US could be forced to leave Europe
squawks.detail: The FT reports that the US President said NATO allies declined to assist in the war with Iran. He also said the US could be forced to leave Europe and called the situation very serious.

squawks.headline: 10-year JGB futures fall 0.22 point in early Tokyo trade ahead of a 20-year bond sale
squawks.detail: Benchmark 10-year Japanese government bond futures fell 0.22 point in early trade. Japan is due to sell 20-year government bonds.

squawks.headline: Trump administration has not approved sending interceptor missiles to Ukraine, Washington Post reports
squawks.detail: According to the Washington Post, the US administration has not approved the transfer of interceptor missiles to Ukraine. Separately, US Vice President Vance said Ukraine should not join NATO.

squawks.headline: UK finance minister Healey rules out raising capital gains tax in the 28 October Budget, the Times reports
squawks.detail: The Times reported on Monday, as cited by Reuters, that John Healey has turned down calls to increase capital gains tax in his first Budget on 28 October. According to the report, he is instead putting economic growth and business investment first.

squawks.headline: Iran's Hormuz management body adds 122 ships to its list of non-compliant vessels
squawks.detail: Iran's Strait of Hormuz Management Organization said it has added 122 ships to its non-compliance list, as Tehran continues to restrict traffic through the strait.

squawks.headline: US Strategic Petroleum Reserve crude stocks fall to 282.7m barrels, the lowest since 1982
squawks.detail: Crude oil held in the US Strategic Petroleum Reserve fell to 282.7 million barrels last week, the lowest level since 1982.

squawks.headline: US lawmakers oppose Trump's proposed Russian diesel deal; European diesel futures have more than doubled this year
squawks.detail: Trump's proposed deal on Russian diesel is meeting opposition from US lawmakers, and analysts question whether extra supply would bring fuel prices down. Brent is up more than 75% this year and European diesel futures have more than doubled.

squawks.headline: Brent settles at $109.55 a barrel, close to a five-month high, as Middle East tensions weigh on supply
squawks.detail: Brent settled at $109.55 a barrel and moved around a five-month high on supply risks from the Middle East. Gains were reported as limited by a recovery in Hormuz flows and by technical indicators showing the market as overbought.

squawks.headline: Ukrainian officials suspect the US is intermittently limiting intelligence sharing; US Secretary of State Rubio denies any pause
squawks.detail: Ukrainian officials say they suspect the US is restricting intelligence sharing on and off, leaving Ukraine without early warning of Russian missile attacks. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio denies there has been any pause in support.

squawks.headline: Iran summons the EU and German ambassadors, reports say
squawks.detail: Reports say Tehran has summoned the ambassadors of the EU and Germany. Earlier, Iran's foreign minister accused European countries of complicity in the US war with Iran.

squawks.headline: US Energy Secretary Wright says no Russian diesel has been released so far
squawks.detail: US Energy Secretary Wright said Russian diesel has not yet been released. He made the remark during continuing US talks with Russia on diesel.

squawks.headline: Zelenskiy says Ukraine could halt strikes on Russian refineries if the US helps supply Patriot missiles
squawks.detail: Ukraine's President Zelenskiy said Kyiv could stop hitting Russian refineries for a period in exchange for US help with Patriot missiles. He also said the Pentagon is delaying missile deliveries under the PURL programme, and called the US decisions hard to explain.

squawks.headline: Trump says he would discuss Ukraine with China's Xi and calls Xi's stance on the war very fair
squawks.detail: US President Trump said he would be willing to talk to Chinese President Xi about Ukraine and described Xi's position on Ukraine as very fair. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Trump says Russia could have done much more to help Iran
squawks.detail: President Trump made the remark in comments to reporters on Monday evening, alongside further remarks on Ukraine and the protests in France. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Trump says it may be time for someone other than Zelenskiy to negotiate on Ukraine's behalf
squawks.detail: US President Trump said Zelenskiy does not know what he is talking about, and that the US shares intelligence with Ukraine and gives it a lot but gets nothing back. In the same remarks he said Russia had done very little to help Iran and called that positive.

squawks.headline: Trump says the US is negotiating with Russia on Iran and diesel and is open to a trilateral meeting with Russia and China
squawks.detail: Speaking live, the US President said he would schedule a joint meeting with Xi and Putin on the basis of denuclearisation, said Russia has been fine on Ukraine, and said he did not think Zelenskiy wants to end the war. No market reaction was reported in the posts.

squawks.headline: Trump says the Iran situation is good, Putin is staying out of Iran and the US is negotiating with Putin on Ukraine
squawks.detail: In remarks on Monday evening, US President Trump said the situation regarding Iran was good and that Putin was leaving Iran alone. He also said Washington was negotiating with Putin on Ukraine and did not want to break off those talks.

squawks.headline: Iran says its offer to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within days still stands if the US accepts its conditions
squawks.detail: Iran said the offer to reopen the strait remains available on condition that Washington accepts Tehran's terms. Tensions and attacks around the waterway are continuing.

squawks.headline: IRGC spokesman points to seven major undersea data cables under the Strait of Hormuz in a warning to Iran's enemies
squawks.detail: Iran's Revolutionary Guards spokesman said seven major cables carrying global internet and business data run beneath the Strait of Hormuz, and told the enemy to bear this in mind, Fars News reported. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Israel's finance minister Smotrich calls for annexing Lebanese territory up to current Israeli lines, and further if Hezbollah attacks
squawks.detail: Israeli Finance Minister Smotrich said Israel should annex Lebanon at least up to where its forces are now positioned, and advance as far as Beirut and beyond if Hezbollah attacks again. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: IRGC spokesman says Iran could widen its blockade beyond Hormuz to the Bab al-Mandeb Strait and the Suez Canal
squawks.detail: The Tehran Times reports an IRGC spokesman as saying Iran has not yet fully closed the Strait of Hormuz and could extend the blockade to the Bab al-Mandeb Strait and the Suez Canal. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: WTI crude settles 2.22% higher at $103.66 a barrel, up $2.25
squawks.detail: NYMEX November WTI futures settled at $103.66 a barrel, up $2.25 or 2.22% on the day. November diesel futures settled at $4.9201 a gallon and November gasoline at $3.1914 a gallon.

squawks.headline: US official denies Iran's claim that US forces struck an Iranian naval base
squawks.detail: A US official told a CNN reporter that Iran's claim that the US had struck one of its naval bases is inaccurate. Iran's navy had earlier said US forces hit its Konark base.

squawks.headline: Germany's Merz says Berlin is committing more than €500bn by the end of the decade to defence and military infrastructure
squawks.detail: German Chancellor Merz described the programme as the biggest modernisation drive in Germany's recent history. In the same remarks he said Russia and its allies, from North Korea to Iran, are attacking post-war democratic values as well as Ukraine.

squawks.headline: Bank of Japan sees inflation close to its 2% target and is preparing a policy pivot, Nikkei reports
squawks.detail: Nikkei reports that the Bank of Japan judges inflation to be near its 2% target and is getting ready for a change in policy direction.

squawks.headline: Iran's President Pezeshkian says Tehran is ready to settle issues with regional countries through dialogue
squawks.detail: Reports say Pezeshkian stated that Iran has no fundamental differences with countries in the region. Separately, Iran told Russia it welcomes any regional peace initiative.

squawks.headline: US Energy Secretary Wright says the US is converting sanctioned dark tankers into legitimate vessels
squawks.detail: US Energy Secretary Wright said sanctioned tankers are being converted into legitimate tankers. He added that the number converted could run from dozens to hundreds.

squawks.headline: Barclays says its £15bn private credit book meets accounting and capital rules after report of Bank of England scrutiny
squawks.detail: Barclays said its £15 billion private credit exposure was treated in line with accounting and regulatory capital requirements, Reuters reports. The statement follows a report that the Bank of England was examining whether the bank's traders had understated the risk.

squawks.headline: US Energy Secretary Wright says talks with the UK on releasing diesel stocks are continuing
squawks.detail: US Energy Secretary Wright said on Monday that discussions with the UK on diesel stock releases are still under way. No figures or timing were given.

squawks.headline: Lyon imposes a city-centre curfew from 9pm Monday to 6am Tuesday as French unrest continues
squawks.detail: The local prefecture announced the overnight curfew in Lyon city centre. It follows curfews already ordered in Paris, Lille and other northern cities after the riots.

squawks.headline: Germany's Merz says there is no rush to decide on ECB posts, though a quick decision could be reached if needed
squawks.detail: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said there is no need for a fast decision on ECB positions, but added that agreement on the jobs could be reached quickly if required.

squawks.headline: Brent turns higher on the day and WTI extends gains after Houthis claim attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure
squawks.detail: Brent was last up 0.15% and WTI up 1.5% after the Houthis said they had attacked Saudi infrastructure. Brent had earlier been down 2.43% on the day, below $105 a barrel.

squawks.headline: French authorities extend curfews to Paris, covering Place de la République and Les Halles from 2000 GMT
squawks.detail: BFM TV reports that French authorities have ordered a curfew for the Place de la République and Les Halles areas of Paris from 2000 GMT. It follows earlier curfews in Lille and other northern cities after riots.

squawks.headline: Netanyahu reportedly tells Trump that Israel still has work to finish
squawks.detail: Israel Hayom reports that Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu told US President Trump that Israel's work is not yet complete. The report comes as US-Iran tensions continue.

squawks.headline: Scotiabank expects the Bank of Canada to raise rates by 25bp next week
squawks.detail: Scotiabank expects a 25bp Bank of Canada hike at next week's decision, a report said.

squawks.headline: Adviser to Iran's supreme leader rejects claims that the Strait of Hormuz is open
squawks.detail: An adviser to Iran's supreme leader said claims that the Strait of Hormuz is open have no basis, Tasnim News reported.

squawks.headline: Netanyahu says Trump sees the final removal of the Iranian threat as the key issue
squawks.detail: Israeli PM Netanyahu referred to Trump's support ahead of Israel's elections and said the final removal of the Iranian threat to Israel is the central question, Israel's Channel 14 News reported.

squawks.headline: Houthis claim strikes on Saudi Arabia's Shaybah oilfield and on airports in Riyadh and Abha
squawks.detail: Yemen's Houthi forces say they attacked the Shaybah oilfield, King Khalid airport in Riyadh and Abha airport. The posts do not report any damage to oil output or any market reaction.

squawks.headline: Houthis say they have attacked Saudi energy, airport and military targets, including an Aramco site in Yanbu
squawks.detail: Yemen's Houthi-run forces announced several military operations deep inside Saudi territory, saying the targets included energy facilities, airports and military sites, among them an Aramco site in Yanbu. The batch reports no market reaction.

squawks.headline: IRGC spokesman says new weapons and targets will be revealed in a new phase of the war with the US
squawks.detail: Fars News reported that a spokesman for Iran's Revolutionary Guards said new weapons and targets would be unveiled and that Iran would drive what is left of US power out of the region.

squawks.headline: France to impose 8pm curfew in Lille and other northern cities after riots, reports say
squawks.detail: Reports say France will bring in an 8pm curfew in Lille and other cities in the north of the country. The government had already ordered partial curfews after the riots.

squawks.headline: Iran's first vice president says Tehran has no choice but to take control of the Strait of Hormuz
squawks.detail: Iran's first vice president Aref, cited by state news agency IRNA, said Iran must assert control over Hormuz, and that passage through the strait can be made easier for friendly nations. The posts report no market reaction.

squawks.headline: Iran's navy says US forces have struck its Konark base
squawks.detail: Iran's navy said US forces had carried out a strike on its Konark base. No market reaction was reported alongside the claim.

squawks.headline: Bank of Canada Q3 business survey indicator improves to -0.33; consumers' five-year inflation expectations rise to 3.91%
squawks.detail: The Bank of Canada's Q3 Business Outlook Survey, mostly conducted before Canada-US trade talks collapsed, shows its indicator at -0.33, up from a revised -0.39 in Q2. The share of firms expecting a recession next year fell to 6% from 17%, and 41% expect inflation above 3% over the next two years, down from 44%. In the separate consumer survey, five-year inflation expectations rose to 3.91% from 3.39%, and 53.0% of Canadians expect a recession, down from 54.6%.

squawks.headline: Bank of Canada business survey shows a weaker outlook and higher inflation expectations after Canada-US trade talks failed
squawks.detail: The Bank of Canada's September survey of business leaders shows firms' outlook got worse. Their inflation expectations rose after Canada-US trade talks broke down.

squawks.headline: Yemen's Houthi-run forces threaten Riyadh and say Saudi oil facilities are targets for their missiles
squawks.detail: A military source with the Houthi-run Yemeni armed forces said the Saudi capital would not be safe and that Saudi oil facilities are within missile range, Iran's Fars news agency reported. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: French 10-year yields on course for their biggest one-day rise since March 2025
squawks.detail: A market newswire headline reports the move as French bond selling continues amid political unrest and rioting. No new yield level was given.

squawks.headline: French 10-year yield climbs further to 4.94%, up 16bp on the day
squawks.detail: French 10-year government bond yields extended their rise to stand 16bp higher at 4.94%. The move follows weekend rioting across France and continuing political instability.

squawks.headline: Violent protests spread from France to Italy and Belgium, with looting and clashes in Milan, Brussels and Liège
squawks.detail: The FT reports looting and clashes with police in Milan, Brussels, Liège and Tirana as unrest spreads beyond France. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: China threatens to retaliate if the UK keeps restrictions on Chinese electric vehicles
squawks.detail: China's Commerce Ministry says it will firmly counter any UK move to press ahead with restrictive measures against Chinese EVs.

squawks.headline: US NAHB housing market index falls to 29 in October, below the 31 forecast and down from 32
squawks.detail: The US NAHB housing market index came in at 29, against a forecast of 31 and a previous reading of 32.

squawks.headline: Russia's Lavrov calls US and Israeli action against Iran baseless and offers help in resolving the crisis
squawks.detail: Russian foreign minister Lavrov said Moscow is ready to help find a way out of the crisis.

squawks.headline: Iran's foreign minister accuses European countries of complicity in the US war with Iran
squawks.detail: Iran's foreign minister Araghchi also said Tehran would welcome any proposal that guarantees regional security without a foreign presence.

squawks.headline: Iran's foreign minister says attacks on ships in the Caspian Sea are a serious concern and calls on Europe to drop double standards
squawks.detail: Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi also said diplomacy is the only route open to the US in the dispute with Iran. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Russia's Lavrov calls for restoring free navigation through Hormuz and says neither Ukraine nor others are ready for talks
squawks.detail: Russian Foreign Minister Lavrov called for a return to pre-crisis conditions in the Middle East, including freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz, and for Yemen negotiations to resume. He said Russia would prefer to reach its goals in Ukraine through talks, that it sticks to its investment and nuclear agreements with Iran, and that it has no interest in volatile energy prices.

squawks.headline: Iran's foreign minister blames the US for Strait of Hormuz tensions and says Iran-US and Ukraine disputes need negotiated settlements
squawks.detail: Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi said the US bears responsibility for insecurity in the Strait of Hormuz and that regional issues should be settled through diplomacy, according to state TV. He said Iran-US talks, Ukraine and the Hormuz situation came up in his discussions, and that both the Ukraine and Iran-US conflicts should be resolved by negotiation rather than war.

squawks.headline: Egypt's parliament delays its vote on military support for Saudi Arabia to 26 October
squawks.detail: Lawmakers said the Egyptian parliament has pushed back to 26 October its vote on letting the armed forces help defend Saudi Arabia against Houthi attacks. The vote had been expected this week.

squawks.headline: Ukraine's foreign minister says Kyiv faces obstacles in getting interceptors against Russian ballistic missiles
squawks.detail: Ukraine's foreign minister said the country is running into obstacles in obtaining interceptors to counter Russian ballistic missiles.

squawks.headline: Chinese Premier urges all sides in the Iran conflict to choose peace and return to talks soon
squawks.detail: According to Xinhua, China's Premier said all parties concerned should opt for peace and resume dialogue and negotiations at an early date. He also said Beijing is ready to advance exchanges and cooperation with Iran.

squawks.headline: Zelenskiy says some types of essential US supplies to Ukraine are being delayed
squawks.detail: Ukraine's president said deliveries of some categories of essential supplies from the US have been delayed. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Egypt's parliament to vote this week on letting its armed forces help defend Saudi Arabia against Houthi attacks
squawks.detail: Reuters reports that Egypt's parliament is expected to vote this week on authorising its military to help defend Saudi Arabia against attacks by Yemen's Houthis. The support would be given if Riyadh asks for it.

squawks.headline: White House adviser Hassett says US inflation appears to need more work again
squawks.detail: White House senior adviser Kevin Hassett said US inflation appears to need further work again. In the same remarks, he described discretionary travel as a sign that consumers feel confident.

squawks.headline: Swap pricing for a Bank of Canada rate hike in October falls to 68% from 74% after Canadian CPI data
squawks.detail: Swap market data put the chance of a Bank of Canada hike in October at 68%, down from 74% before the September inflation release.

squawks.headline: Canadian CPI rises 0.1% m/m in September, below the 0.2% forecast; CPI-trim slows to 1.8% and CPI-common to 2.4%
squawks.detail: Canada's September CPI rose 0.1% on the month against a 0.2% forecast, after -0.1% previously. CPI-trim came in at 1.8% (forecast 1.9%, previous 1.9%), CPI-common at 2.4% (previous 2.6%) and BoC core CPI at 2.2% y/y (previous 2.4%), with core flat on the month.

squawks.headline: Canadian CPI rises 3.1% y/y, below the 3.2% forecast; CPI-median measure at 1.9%
squawks.detail: Canada's annual CPI came in at 3.1%, against a 3.2% forecast and up from 3.0% previously. The CPI-median core measure was 1.9%, against a 2% forecast and down from 2.0%.

squawks.headline: Resolution Foundation says UK household energy bills are due to rise again in January
squawks.detail: The Resolution Foundation says the next rise in household energy bills is due in January. It notes that 46% of domestic gas use falls in the first quarter of the year.

squawks.headline: Iraq's October oil exports average over 3.4m b/d so far, up from 3m b/d in September, reports say
squawks.detail: Reports put Iraq's crude exports at an average of more than 3.4 million barrels per day so far in October, compared with 3 million barrels per day in September.

squawks.headline: IRGC spokesman warns that even limited US action against Iran would set off a global energy crisis
squawks.detail: A spokesman for Iran's Revolutionary Guards gave the warning, Sepah News reported. No market reaction was reported in the posts.

squawks.headline: French PM says intelligence agencies warn the far left could try to disrupt the presidential election
squawks.detail: French PM Lecornu says intelligence agencies have briefed him on the risk. Separately, President Macron condemns looting and vandalism during cost-of-living protests and orders a review of intelligence and police preparedness.

squawks.headline: Iranian hardliners call for nuclear weapons after the killing of Supreme Leader Khamenei, FT reports
squawks.detail: The Financial Times reports that hardliners in Iran are pushing to weaponise the enrichment programme. They say Khamenei, who had prohibited atomic bombs, has been killed.

squawks.headline: French PM Lecornu says the government would declare a state of emergency if it were judged necessary
squawks.detail: France's prime minister made the remark as rioting continues across the country. French bonds have already been under selling pressure today because of the unrest.

squawks.headline: Report says a breakthrough to halt US-Iran escalation is expected to be announced this week
squawks.detail: A market newswire reports that mediators are still working to narrow the points of contention between the US and Iran. The report names no source, and no market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: French PM Lecornu orders partial curfews after riots and says the finance ministry can fully fund short-time working
squawks.detail: French Prime Minister Lecornu said he had asked prefectures and some local authorities to impose partial curfews tonight, that the government will support business, and that the finance ministry can fund short-time working at 100%. He said about 80% of those still in custody will be prosecuted.

squawks.headline: Kremlin says a proposed Putin-Trump-Xi summit has no agenda or substantive agreements yet and a Ukraine deal needs Kyiv's participation
squawks.detail: The Kremlin said there is no agenda yet for the proposed summit of Putin, Trump and Xi, and no substantive agreements have been reached. It also said a final peace settlement for Ukraine is hardly possible unless someone from Kyiv's side takes part.

squawks.headline: French borrowing costs rise 0.1 percentage point as bond selling resumes; 10-year spread over Germany back at 1.45 percentage points
squawks.detail: The FT reports that French government bonds are under renewed selling pressure today, lifting borrowing costs by 0.1 percentage point. That takes the extra yield France pays over Germany on 10-year debt back up to 1.45 percentage points.

squawks.headline: Chancellor Healey reportedly weighs income tax on family business handovers before his first Budget
squawks.detail: City AM, citing a report, says Chancellor John Healey is considering charging income tax when owners pass companies to their children, which could nearly double the tax bill. The report says the plans are aimed at avoiding spending cuts.

squawks.headline: Ukraine's foreign minister says a Russia-China-US summit would only encourage Putin to keep fighting
squawks.detail: Ukraine's foreign minister criticised the proposed summit of Russia, China and the US, saying it would encourage Putin to continue the war. This follows reports that Putin has proposed a summit with Trump and Xi on Ukraine's future.

squawks.headline: PBOC governor says the bank will study moving its main open market operation tenor to overnight at an appropriate time
squawks.detail: China's central bank governor said the change would aim to make interest rate regulation more precise, according to Chinese state media.

squawks.headline: Trafigura economist puts Middle East crude flows 5m-7m b/d below pre-war levels and product flows 4m b/d lower
squawks.detail: The chief economist at commodity trader Trafigura gave the estimates for reduced Middle East crude and oil product flows compared with before the war.

squawks.headline: PBOC governor widens eligibility for standing lending facilities and plans to let overseas institutions trade RMB onshore
squawks.detail: The People's Bank of China governor also announced steps to promote bond market connectivity and to make it easier for overseas financial institutions to trade renminbi in China's domestic foreign exchange market, CCTV reported. The measures were announced alongside the liquidity support tool for non-bank institutions.

squawks.headline: PBOC governor says China will launch a liquidity support tool for large-scale redemptions at non-bank institutions
squawks.detail: The People's Bank of China governor announced plans for a liquidity facility to support non-bank financial institutions facing large-scale redemptions. No size or timing was given.

squawks.headline: Goldman Sachs says its cross-asset sentiment and positioning gauge falls to its lowest since April
squawks.detail: Goldman Sachs says its sentiment and positioning indicator has fallen to its lowest level since April and has decoupled from strong global PMIs. The bank points to stronger fixed income fund flows, positioning in gold and the yen, and a sharp fall in hedge fund net leverage.

squawks.headline: US Secretary of State Rubio says Ukraine and Russia should concentrate on ending the war
squawks.detail: Rubio made the remarks on arriving in Uzbekistan for meetings with officials of the C5+1 grouping of the US and post-Soviet Central Asian states, Reuters reports.

squawks.headline: UBS now expects the ECB to raise rates by 25bp in March 2027 after a December hike
squawks.detail: UBS has changed its ECB call. It previously expected the hiking cycle to end in December and now also expects a 25bp increase in March 2027.
